title: Reliably Engineering and Controlling Stable Optogenetic Gene Circuits in Mammalian Cells
protocol: Select genetic components to combine into a single gene circuit/plasmid.
Store DNA sequences using genetic engineering and/or molecular cloning software.
Annotate each DNA sequence.
Examine necessary features such as START codons, regulatory sequences, or translated sequences.
Develop or adopt parts according to the overall gene circuit design.
Fuse a gene sequence coding for a domain capable of light-inducible degradation adjacent to and in the frame of the repressor gene.
Ensure the presence of an activator domain that promotes gene expression upon light-induced DNA binding.
Include regulatory binding sites in or upstream of the regulator gene's promoter for negative or positive autoregulation.
Design primers for DNA sequence amplification or sequencing of the plasmid using molecular cloning software.
Validate primers computationally through built-in features of molecular cloning software.
Order oligonucleotide primers from the manufacturer.
Dilute primers to a 100 mM stock concentration in double-distilled water.
Dilute 100 mM stock primers to a 10 mM concentration for PCR.
Prepare the PCR mix with 1 µL of forward primer, 1 µL of reverse primer, and 1 µL of template DNA.
Add ddH2O to reach a total reaction volume of 25 µL in the PCR mix.
Incubate the PCR mix in a thermocycler for initial denaturation at 95 °C for 30 s.
Cycle through 40 cycles with denaturation at 98 °C for 5 s, annealing at 65 °C for 30 s, and extension at 72 °C for 1 min.
Perform a final extension cycle of 2 min at 72 °C.
Hold the reaction at 4 °C until gel electrophoresis can be performed.
Repeat step 1.9 to amplify all the fragments for DNA assembly reaction.
Run PCR products on a 1% agarose gel.
Purify bands of desired length from the gel.
Prepare master mix for DNA assembly reaction according to Table 1 instructions.
Incubate DNA assembly reaction master mix in thermocycler at 50 °C for 1 h.
Store DNA assembly reaction at 4 °C.
Set up bacterial transformation using competent E. coli cells and appropriate protocol.
Plate the transformation mix on LB agar plates containing selection marker (e.g., Ampicillin).
Incubate plates at 37 °C overnight.
Inoculate colonies by picking individual colonies from plates.
Resuspend colonies in liquid LB broth with corresponding antibiotic in culture tubes.
Incubate culture tubes in shaker incubator at 37 °C, 300 rpm overnight.
Perform plasmid preparation protocol to extract plasmid DNA from bacterial culture.
Validate the circuit in two steps.
Perform a test digestion using restriction enzymes as a crude verification.
Select at least two restriction enzymes that produce at least two fragments.
Prepare the test samples by adding 1 µL of each enzyme, 5 µL of the generated DNA, and 13 µL of water with appropriate salts and buffers depending on the enzymes used.
Incubate the reaction at 37 °C for 1 h, or as the enzyme manufacturer suggests.
Run the test digestion products on a 1% agarose gel.
Determine whether the bands are correct.
If the bands are correct, proceed to sequencing.
Generate primers based on the DNA stored in the software so that the annealing regions of the primers are about 500 bp apart and cover the fragment of interest or the full plasmid.
Dilute the primers with pure nuclease-free water (NF-H2O) to 10 mM concentration.
Prepare the sequencing samples by adding 1 µL of 10 ng/µL DNA, 1 µL of primer, and 8 µL of NF-H2O to a 0.2 mL tube.
Repeat this for each primer.
Order a mammalian cell line for rapid generation of stable sub-lines ensuring high-level expression from a mammalian expression vector.
Grow cells in 5% CO2 in humidified air at 37 °C, adjusting growth conditions as needed for the cell type.

Transfect the gene circuits designed above into the desired cells obtained previously to begin a stable cell-line generation process using a liposome mixture of gene circuit DNA with appropriate recombinase or through other methods such as electroporation.
Split cells to 25% confluency two days after transfection.
Exchange media six hours after splitting with fresh media containing 50 µg/mL of hygromycin antibiotic (or another appropriate antibiotic).
Change media every 2-3 days in the presence of antibiotic until a few dozen foci appear on the plate or flask.
Trypsinize cells with 1 mL of 0.25% trypsin, 0.1% EDTA in HBSS without Calcium, Magnesium, and Sodium Bicarbonate for several minutes.
Neutralize trypsin with fresh media.
Pass all cells into a fresh container.
Once the cells in the fresh container are 80%-100% confluent, mix them with a solution of 45% old media, 45% fresh media, and 10% DMSO to freeze them down.
Transfer remaining cells into a sterile tube for single-cell sorting.
Isolate monoclonal cells from the sorted cells into wells in a 96-well plate.
Split cells into a 12-well plate when approximately 50%-60% confluent.
Once the 12-well plate is 80%-100% confluent, split the cells into a tissue culture treated T-25 flask.
When the cells in the T-25 flask are 80%-100% confluent, freeze them for characterization and testing of monoclonal cell lines.
Characterize the monoclonal cell lines by microscopy to report gene expression profiles based on induced fluorescent reporter production.
Verify functional protein production via fluorescent antibody labeling and immunofluorescence assay.
Test transcriptional-level gene expression induction via quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR).
Validate genetic sequence and integration accuracy via local and whole-genome sequencing of the clones.
Construct 3D parts as outlined in Gerhardt et al. (2016 and 2019).
Assemble the circuit board according to Gerhardt et al. (2016 and 2019).
Program the assembled LPA circuit using a microcontroller programmer as described in Gerhardt et al. (2016 and 2019).
Combine 3D printed parts with the assembled circuit board.
Mount the plate adaptor, LED spacer, mounting plate, circuit board, 24-well plate, and plate lid together using mounting bolts and wing nuts.
Program an SD card for the Light Plate Apparatus (LPA) using IRIS software available on the Tabor Lab website.
Calibrate the finished device.
Choose the LPA (4 x 6) option from the drop-down menu.
Select the Steady-state illumination approach.
Enter values in the cells corresponding to the wells of the plate for top LEDs.
Program blue LEDs placed at the top position.
Set light intensity levels using grayscale units.
Enter 8 different light intensities with three technical replicates per plate.
Design IRIS experimental files considering edge effects from adjacent wells on the LPA device.
Minimize light crosstalk and heat influence on adjacent wells by implementing a randomization matrix in the IRIS software.
Scramble well locations to reduce edge effects.
Mitigate light toxicity by producing a response curve for light intensity, pulse duration, or duty cycle based on the modality being investigated.
Program 8 light intensity values with three replicates per 24-well plate, ranging from no light to maximum intensity of the LPA.
Run samples on a flow cytometer using an SSC-FSC gate or live stain such as propidium iodide.
Quantify cell survival at each light value.
Determine the ideal amount of population survival for the experimental setup.
Set 80% cell survival as an appropriate tradeoff.
Calibrate the intensity to not exceed 3000 g.s. units.
Restrict light values to avoid toxicity.
Characterize a particular part of the dose-response range.
Scan a wide range of light intensities, pulse durations, or duty cycles to determine the desired dose-response.
Program a single LPA with up to 24 wells for different intensity/pulse duration/duty cycle settings.
Proceed with cell culture work or assays using the determined optimal light regime.
Characterize an optogenetic system by testing a wide range of light stimuli.
Determine the range interval that gives the desired gene expression response.
Perform subsequent experiments in the refined dose range based on initial characterization.
Use 3000 g.s. units as the upper bound for assays like immunofluorescence if determined to be the toxic light intensity threshold.
Calibrate the LPA using an Image analysis method if not already done.
Program the LPA with a value of 2000 g.s.
Press the reset button on the LPA after programming.
Acquire an image of the entire device.
Rotate the device by 180° and acquire another image.
Use open-source software to calculate LED compensation values.
Proceed to cell culture work for initiation of light-induction assay.
Obtain flasks of engineered monoclonal cells from the previous section.
Remove old media from the flask.
Add 1 mL of trypsin to the cells.
Incubate for 5 min.
Neutralize trypsin by adding 4 mL of DMEM supplemented with hygromycin, penicillin/streptomycin solution, and fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Seed ~75,000 cells per well in a 24-well black plate.
Add the cell suspension to achieve a total volume of 500 µL per well.
Place the plates in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2 for 2-6 hours.
Transfer the cells to a tissue culture hood after incubation.
Remove the plastic lid from the plate.
Attach an adhesive foil strip to the top of the plate.
Place the plate in the fitted 3D parts of the LPA.
Cover the plate with the 3D-printed LPA lid that fits over the device screws on each corner.
Plug the device into the power source.
Push the reset button on the LPA device to ensure updated experiment settings are applied.
Incubate the cells within the experimental system for an appropriate amount of time, depending on the original seeding density, cell line-specific growth speed, and growth conditions.
Remove the cells in the LPA from the incubator 24-72 h post-induction.
Place them in a tissue culture hood.
Remove the foil strip.
Let the plate sit for 1-2 min to prevent condensation on the plastic lid.
Put the original plastic lid back on the plate after 1-2 min of sitting.
Image the cells with the appropriate phase contrast or fluorescence microscope.
Adjust the exposure time, light source intensity, and gain for displaying engineered cells.
Apply 50 ms exposure time for FITC/GFP light source.
Set phase-contrast exposure time at 1-5 ms.
Maintain phase-contrast light source intensity at 100%.
Optimize parameters to minimize oversaturation in the fluorescence reporter.
Minimize cellular damage during imaging.
Capture adequate images for qualitative and quantitative analysis.
Maximize signal-to-noise ratios when setting parameters.
Minimize phototoxicity effects on cells.
Increase ability to amplify weak fluorescence signals.
Program a coordinate template into the microscopy software for plate imaging.
Remove cells from LPA in the incubator or microscope after imaging and place them in the tissue culture hood.
If removing directly from LPA, remove the foil strip and let the plate sit for 1-2 minutes.
Aspirate media from each well of a 24-well plate if all wells are used.
Add 100 µL of 0.25% trypsin to each well, cover with plastic lid, and return to incubator.
Leave cells undisturbed in the incubator for 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes, remove the plate from the incubator.
Neutralize each trypsinized well with 400 µL of DMEM.
Label a 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tube with cell strainer corresponding to each well.
Use a P1000 pipette to pipette contents of each well up and down 6-8 times to break cell clumps.
Transfer entire contents of each well (~500 µL) to the labeled tubes with the strainer.
Bring cells to the appropriate flow cytometry instrument with lasers of the correct wavelengths.

Create a forward- and side-scatter gate (FSC and SSC, respectively) on the flow cytometry software to capture single cells of the appropriate size and granularity, excluding debris and cellular clumps.
Capture approximately 10,000 cells with the set gate.
Import the data to available flow cytometry data software for analysis.
Create an FSC-SSC gate and apply it to each batch of experimental data.
Plot the flow cytometry data as histograms or represent in other ways to illustrate the obtained expression patterns.
Remove cells from the LPA in the incubator or microscope after imaging and place them in the tissue culture hood.
If removed directly from the LPA, remove the foil strip and let the plate sit for 1-2 minutes.
Aspirate the media from each well of the entire 24-well plate if all wells are used.
Extract RNA from the cells using an appropriate RNA extraction kit.
Perform a reverse transcription reaction of each sample.
Set up PCR reactions with DNA polymerase according to the associated protocol.
Utilize a housekeeping gene and a gene of interest in a multiplexed reaction or create separate reactions.
Probe for GFP, KRAS, and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) levels via qRT-PCR.
Analyze qRT-PCR data using available software to illustrate gene circuit fold change at the RNA level.
Add 100 μL of 0.25% trypsin to each well.
Cover the plate with a plastic lid.
Place the plate back in the incubator.
Incubate undisturbed for 5 minutes.
Remove the plate from the incubator and place it in the tissue culture hood.
Neutralize each trypsinized well with 400 μL of DMEM.
Label mini-centrifuge tubes corresponding to each well.
Use a P1000 pipette to mix contents of each well up and down 6-8 times.
Transfer the entire contents of each well (~500 μL) to labeled tubes.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 400 x g.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 750-1000 µL of 4% paraformaldehyde diluted in PBS.
Incubate the cells for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Add 750-1000 μL of PBS to each tube.
Pipette up and down several times.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 400 x g.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 750-1000 µL of ice-cold methanol.
Incubate on ice or in a -20 °C freezer for 30 minutes.
Add 750-1000 μL of PBS to each tube after incubation.
Pipette up and down several times.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 400 x g.
Discard the supernatant.
Move the samples to a chemical fume hood.
Resuspend the cells using a P1000/P200 pipette.
Pipette up and down 6-8 times in each tube to break cell clumps.
Dilute primary antibodies at a ratio of 1:800 in an incubation buffer made from 1x PBS with 0.5 g of BSA.
Incubate the tubes for 1 hour at room temperature.
Cover the tubes with foil.
Add 750-1000 µL of the incubation buffer to each tube after antibody addition.
Pipette up and down several times.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 400 x g.
Discard the supernatant.
Move the samples to a chemical fume hood.
Resuspend the cells using a P1000/P200 pipette and pipette up and down 6-8 times in each tube to break cell clumps in 100 µL of secondary antibody.
Cover the tubes with foil to prevent light effects on labeled antibodies.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Add 750-1000 µL of incubation buffer.
Pipette up and down several times.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 400 x g.
Discard the supernatant.
Move the samples to a chemical fume hood.
Resuspend the cells using a P1000 pipette and pipette up and down 6-8 times in each tube in 500 µL of PBS.
Transfer the entire contents of each tube (~500 µL) to labeled tubes with strainers.
Resuspend cells using a P1000/P200 pipette in 100 µL of labeled primary antibody and pipette up and down 6-8 times in each tube to break cell clumps.
Determine appropriate antibody dilution from the standard curve empirically.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature covered with foil.
Add 750-1000 µl of incubation buffer after incubation and pipette up and down several times.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 400 x g.
Resuspend the cells using a P1000 pipette in 500 μL of PBS and pipette up and down 6-8 times to break cell clumps.
Transfer the entire contents of each tube (~500 µl) to labeled tubes with strainers.
Bring the cells to appropriate flow cytometry instruments with lasers of the correct wavelengths.
